title: Carry-lookahead finally clicked and I feel stupid for how long it took
author: nandhole
body:
Spent about three weeks on and off being confused about why generate/propagate is a thing, and I think the textbooks bury the lede.

The thing nobody said plainly: **a ripple-carry adder is slow because bit `i` cannot start until bit `i-1` finishes.** That's it. That's the whole problem. Everything else is just algebra to break that chain.

Once you accept that, G and P are obvious:

```
g[i] = a[i] AND b[i]     // this bit MAKES a carry, no matter what came in
p[i] = a[i] XOR b[i]     // this bit PASSES a carry through, if one arrives
```

And then `c[i+1] = g[i] OR (p[i] AND c[i])` which you can just... keep substituting into itself until `c[i]` is gone. Expand it for four bits and every carry is a function of the inputs only. No chain.

The cost is that the gates get wide fast. `c[4]` needs a 5-input OR and one of its AND terms has 5 inputs. That's why real designs do it in blocks of 4 and then lookahead across the blocks.

Anyway. If you're stuck on this, the question to ask isn't "what is generate", it's "what exactly is the dependency I'm trying to delete".

replies.author: segfaulter
replies.body:
The block-of-4 detail is the part I wish I'd known earlier. You can treat a whole 4-bit block as having its own G and P and then run the exact same lookahead one level up. It's recursive and nobody tells you.

Group generate for a 4-block:

```
G = g3 | (p3 & g2) | (p3 & p2 & g1) | (p3 & p2 & p1 & g0)
P = p3 & p2 & p1 & p0
```

Same shape as the single-bit version. That's the whole trick for 32 and 64 bit adders.

replies.author: carry_the_one
replies.body:
fwiw the reason p is XOR and not OR: you also use p as the sum bit (`sum[i] = p[i] XOR c[i]`), so XOR saves you a gate. If you only cared about the carry logic, OR would work fine there since the case where both are 1 is already covered by g.

Took me ages to notice that's an optimisation and not a requirement.
